clauses.reason: The sole paragraph closes the offices “shall be closed one-half day on Friday, December 24, 1948” and excuses employees “shall be excused from duty for one-half day on December 24,1948”. Both commands are limited to December 24, 1948, so the clause ended on that day by its own terms. The date is recorded inclusive (the order runs through the end of December 24, 1948); the exclusive reading would end it when that day begins. The end source is the order's own text.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 10019 (13 FR 7395 (Federal Register of December 4, 1948)) was signed December 2, 1948. Its held Federal Register text prints the order number, the title and the signing date. Its only paragraph orders that the executive departments, independent establishments and other agencies in the District of Columbia metropolitan area “shall be closed one-half day on Friday, December 24, 1948”, and that employees in the metropolitan area and in the field service, except those excluded by agency heads for special public reasons or whose absence would be inconsistent with existing law, “shall be excused from duty for one-half day on December 24,1948”. On 2026-10-14 the clause is terminated by its own terms: it applies to the single named day, December 24, 1948, and has no operation after that day. The order contains no other command, no condition and no continuing duty. A search of the held texts for the order's number found only the order's own Federal Register page. The Federal Register disposition-note, U.S. Code and eCFR citation searches report no hit naming this order.
